A seat is one engraved pillar on the national triangulation register. The applicant files the designation, coordinates and a photo of the inscription; the node rejects a designation claimed before and each year wants a closed triangle, angles to two neighbouring pillars. Gusts past gale force void a reading, since the theodolite shifts, so the node sets the window.

Fifty clones need fifty pillars: monument 1,100 dollars, permit 700, theodolite 6,400, near 480,000 dollars.

A reef enters the chart when bearings from three hills meet at one vertex; a copied bearing meets nothing.
